title: Style Profile (clean-room, non-runtime style-intake contract)
description: Clean-room, idea-only BRAND / STYLE intake shape for szh-ppt-master. A style_profile captures the abstract design direction a deck should follow — palette, background mode, a typography scale, recurring page motifs, the layout archetypes the style supports, and an image-usage policy that biases the deck toward editable shapes / tables / KPI structures over generated images. It is the next quality layer ABOVE the existing runtime design_system tokens, NOT a runtime application contract: no script projects a style_profile onto a design_system today, so every profile pins runtime_status to the literal non_runtime_contract. The schema deliberately refuses real-brand wording, URL- and path-shaped values, and trademark punctuation at the field-shape level (same gates as schemas/brand_preset.schema.json). It carries no proprietary assets, no copied template slides, and no public URLs. The image_usage_policy block STRUCTURALLY encodes that generated images are auxiliary: its mode enum has no image-first option and editable_structures_first is locked true. This schema uses only the JSON Schema keyword subset that scripts/validate_artifacts.py implements. See references/strategy-and-style-layer.md for the policy envelope.

schema_version.description: Profile schema version. Locked to '1'; bumped only with a paired contract change.

profile_id.description: Stable identifier. Forced to start with the literal prefix 'synthetic_' so a profile can never be authored under a real brand id; the rest is lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscore. The prefix is a fail-closed gate against real-brand authorship at the schema layer.

display_name.description: Human-readable label. The pattern excludes punctuation that real brand marks frequently use (trademark glyphs, parentheses, ampersand, dot, comma, slash, colon) and excludes URL-like shapes.

runtime_status.description: Hard literal. There is no 'runtime' / 'applied' state today — no script projects a style_profile onto a design_system. The literal locks the document at the shape-only contract layer.

palette.description: Closed set of palette tokens. The token NAMES are fixed and the VALUES are constrained to 6-digit hex colours so neither URLs nor named-brand colour wording can slip in. Mirrors schemas/design_system.schema.json so a future projection helper would be straightforward.

background_mode.description: Closed enum describing how slide backgrounds are filled. Abstract design modes only — no proprietary background asset is referenced. 'solid' = flat fill; 'subtle_tint' = near-background tint; 'gradient_band' = a single banded gradient region; 'paneled' = a divided panel block.

typography_scale.description: A modular type scale. heading/body each carry a CSS-style font fallback chain plus a positive point size; scale_ratio is the step multiplier between scale levels. The font_family pattern excludes URL- and path-shaped values.

font_family.description: CSS-style fallback chain, preferred -> fallback. Only ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, and a single space inside each entry; excludes ':' '/' '?' '#' '\\' and quotes.

scale_ratio.description: Modular-scale step multiplier between levels (e.g. 1.25). 1 = no scaling; capped at 2.

page_motifs.description: Closed enum set of recurring, abstract decoration motifs the style reuses across pages. No proprietary graphic asset is referenced — each motif is drawable from the controlled render primitives (shapes / lines / text).

layout_archetypes.description: The visual-structure archetypes this style supports. Shares the exact vocabulary used by strategy_plan.slides[].visual_structure so a future validator can cross-check that every planned slide's structure is one the chosen style declares.

image_usage_policy.description: Policy that biases the deck toward editable structures over generated images. STRUCTURALLY encodes that images are auxiliary: 'mode' has no image-first option and editable_structures_first is locked true.

mode.description: How much the style leans on generated images. 'auxiliary' = occasional spot illustration; 'minimal' = rare; 'none' = editable structures only. There is intentionally NO image-first / image-primary option.

max_image_slides_ratio.description: Soft upper bound on the fraction of slides that may carry a generated image. A small value (e.g. 0.25) keeps most slides on editable shapes / tables / KPI structures.

editable_structures_first.description: Locked true. Asserts that editable shapes, tables, and KPI structures are the primary visual vehicle and generated images are auxiliary.

notes.description: Optional short author note. Keep it terse and synthetic; no real-brand wording, URLs, or path-shaped values.
